Achieve higher power density with TI's AC/DC products, leveraging options from highly integrated GaN devices to flexible PWM controllers
parametric-filter

TI offers AC/DC power conversion products across diverse topologies and applications. Our switching regulators offer improved electrical characterisitics for enhanced efficiency across line and load conditions, meeting modern power supply requirements. TI's converters offer the highest level of integration and enable design simplicity by combining the controller and gallium nitride (GaN) power stage into a single product. Our application-specific controllers integrate gate drivers and use soft-switching controlalgorithms without integrated power transistor. While the general-purpose controllers offer more topology flexibility with drop-in or pin-to-pin replacements. From mobile adapters to electric vehicle chargers, smart TV to datacenter server supplies, and energy infrastructure, TI's AC/DC switching regulators enable breakthrough performance in energy-crititcal applications worldwide.

DDR VDDQ and VTT devices feature low internal references to regulate low DDR core and termination output voltages. Compared to standard linear and switching regulators, DDR terminators can sink or source termination current, and have current capability and external reference inputs to track the VDDQ/2 input and generate the VTT termination rail.

High-side switches and controllers drive capacitive, inductive and resistive loads across automotive and industrial applications. TI's portfolio includes internal-FET and external-FET configurations, providing robust protection and diagnostics across a wide range of load currents. Smart eFuse high-side switches, available in both FET configurations, include additional I2T-based overcurrent protection for protecting wire harnesses. TI's high-side portfolio includes single, dual, and quad-channel configurations with parallel and serial interfaces. Our 12V, 24V and 48V portfolios are tailored to support automotive zone, body, and battery management systems, as well as industrial automation, robotics and energy infrastructure.

These devices reduce both system size and cost while meeting creepage and clearance requirements.

Key technologies of high-side power switches
Simplify your system by reducing PCB traces and eliminating external sensing components
TI high-side switches help protect against high inrush current, overload and short-circuit conditions with adjustable current limiting. Integrating the adjustable current limit reduces PCB traces and connector sizes to lower your system costs. Additionally, accurate current sensing enables real-time monitoring of system loads through open load detection without calibration and eliminates the need for additional sensing components.

Harness the power of integrated wire protection
With the growing power demands of modern vehicles there is a need for greater optimization in energy and material usage. The smart eFuse high-side switch enables power and material savings with its integrated and programmable I2T overcurrent protection curve. This variable curve replicates the energy limits of traditional melting fuses but uses instant-read current sense. The advantage of this solution is multifold:
Instant protection as opposed to a fuse's thermal latency.
Software-resettable fuse that does not need to be physically replaced.
Fuse protection decentralized from the fuse box.

Reduce control signals and enable greater customization
TI's high-side switch portfolio offers two control methods: GPIO or Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI). SPI enables greater customization, allowing the user to control functions like:
Enabling the switches and diagnostics.
Measuring voltage, current and temperature.
Managing faults.
Configuring the current limit and inrush current time.
High-side switches with SPI often integrate an analog-to-digital converter (ADC) to enable the measurement and reporting of signals like temperature, supply voltage and output voltage. The ability to report current-sense data and fault information via SPI helps users identify problems quickly and analyze potential root cause.
